meta.description: Controls error rates across thousands of simultaneous tests in genomics discovery using false-discovery-rate methods (Benjamini-Hochberg, Benjamini-Yekutieli, Storey q-value with pi0 estimation, local FDR, independent filtering, covariate-weighted FDR via IHW), plus family-wise error control (Bonferroni, Holm) and the GWAS genome-wide threshold. Use when correcting p-values from genome-wide tests, choosing between BH/BY/q-value/Bonferroni, setting an FDR threshold, applying IHW or independent filtering, or interpreting q-values.

scientific_integrity.detail: The new Benjamini & Yekutieli 2005 (JASA 100:71-93) citation added for the FCR fix is a real, correctly attributed paper; its formula (1 - alpha*R/m) was run verbatim here and independently improved coverage from 68.9% to 95.6% on a freshly simulated selected set. No fabricated DOI, PMID, p-value or effect size found anywhere in the fixed Skill.

practice_boundaries.detail: Nothing in the Skill or in any of the seven re-audit outputs diagnoses, prescribes or triages an individual; all seven inputs are population-level error-rate questions.

methodological_ground.detail: The rewritten 'Dependence' section is now honest and independently verified: across 1,800 replicate datasets run in this re-audit (300 per structure/method, a different seed and simulation construction than either the pre-fix audit or the fixer used), BH's mean realized FDP never exceeded nominal (0.0446/0.0382/0.0446 across independent/positive-block/negative-pair), while SD(FDP) widened under positive dependence (0.0114->0.0516) and BY's power cost matched the stated ~50% (0.597->0.283, a 52.6% loss). This is the exact claim the pre-fix audit flagged as miscalibrated, and it is now correct.

code_usability.detail: Every code block in the fixed Skill runs: BH, q-value with the lambda=0 fallback (0/600 errors across m=10/20/50 in this re-audit), the FCR-adjustment block (run verbatim, restored coverage), and the IHW section including its documented child-process retry+fallback pattern, verified crash-free at the parent-process level across all runs performed here. The bare ihw() one-liner still crashes the R session at a real, now-honestly-quantified rate (6/12 = 50% in this re-audit's own repeated single-attempt test) -- recorded as a P1, not a veto, because the Skill's own text puts the safe pattern immediately below the risky one-liner and the retry+fallback path is proven to work.

functional_suitability.note: The FCR gap this Skill was previously docked for is closed: a runnable code block now exists where only a name did before, verified in this re-audit to move coverage from 68.9% to 95.6%. Local FDR (qobj$lfdr) still ships with no threshold-interpretation rule, and IDR remains a single taxonomy row with no code -- the same completeness gap the frontmatter's breadth still promises.

reliability.note: This is the category the fix pass targeted directly, and it shows: q-value, IHW and the BH/BY dependence rule -- the three methods with no failure-mode coverage before -- now each have an accurate, tested entry. The IHW entry is the one residual weakness: it documents and mitigates a real crash risk it cannot eliminate, which is honest but still a live risk for an agent that copies only the one-liner.

performance_context.note: 261 lines (up from 192), still dense and table-driven with no filler; the growth is entirely new failure-mode and FCR content, not padding. No references/ directory to defer depth into.

agent_usability.note: Decision tree and taxonomy remain the strongest part and are now internally consistent with the corrected dependence and IHW claims. The IHW code snippet's `de_table` is still referenced without being defined in the same block -- unchanged from the pre-fix version.

human_usability.note: Discoverability unchanged and strong. Forgiveness improved materially: the q-value section now states a family-size floor and shows a working fallback in the same code block the agent will copy, rather than leaving the analyst to discover the spline error alone.

security.note: The new child-process retry pattern (system2() calling Rscript with a fixed, non-user-controlled expression string, writing to tempfile() paths and unlink()-ing them) introduces no injection surface -- verified by inspection and by grep for eval/exec/credential patterns across all three files, one hit (unlink() cleanup, benign). maintainability.note: The IHW section is now testable in the way the rest of the Skill always was: examples/multiple_testing_correction.R ships a real retry+fallback pattern that this re-audit ran seven times without one parent-process crash. One P2 remains untouched by design (per the fix log): the shipped example's BH step still prints a realized FDR of 0.108 against a nominal 0.05 on its own fixed seed, reproduced identically in this re-audit, which still teaches the wrong lesson about the method the Skill recommends.

agent_specific.note: Unchanged best-in-class routing, composability and escape hatches; all seven sibling-skill paths re-verified to exist in the fork at commit 1f9a730. final.grade_note: All floors clear for Production Ready: static 90 >= 80, execution average 88.0 >= 85, Layer 1 average 36.3/40 >= 32, Layer 2 average 51.7/60 >= 48, assertion pass rate 29/31 = 93.5% >= 90%. This is a genuine jump from the pre-fix audit's 82 (Beta Only, not deployable): the pre-fix downgrade was driven entirely by the assertion pass rate (21/33 = 63.6%, below even the 80% Limited-Release floor), and the fix pass closed exactly the gaps that were failing those assertions -- q-value, IHW and BH/BY dependence now have accurate, tested documentation where before they had none or had a miscalibrated claim. No veto fired and no safety or scope assertion failed on any input.

key_strengths: All 4 open P1s from the pre-fix audit are genuinely resolved, independently reproduced with fresh data, different seeds and (for two of them) a different simulation construction than either the pre-fix audit or the fixer used: the BH/BY dependence section is now factually accurate (5/5 assertions pass, up from 3/5), the q-value lambda=0 fallback had 0 errors across 600 replicates at m=10/20/50, the FCR-adjustment code block moved coverage from 68.9% to 95.6%, and the IHW section is now honestly caveated with a proven-working retry+fallback pattern.

The fix pass is unusually honest about what it did NOT fix: SKILL.md now states the IHW crash is reduced but not eliminated (independently confirmed at 6/12 = 50%, exactly matching the stated range) and that pi0.method='bootstrap' does not actually help (independently confirmed: identical failure counts to the default estimator, just a different error) -- neither claim overstates the fix, which is itself evidence of a trustworthy Skill.

Two genuinely new probes beyond anything the fixer was told about both confirmed deep, specific technical claims rather than surface-level ones: IHW's nbins==1 collapse-to-BH is not just asserted but numerically identical to BH's output on live data, and the Skill's guidance against pi0.method='bootstrap' holds up when a user actively proposes it as a fix.

Zero parent-R-session crashes were observed across every run of the shipped example's retry+fallback pattern in this re-audit, including a run where the underlying solver failed all 3 retries and the code fell back to BH cleanly and correctly.

recommendations.title: The bare IHW one-liner in the code block is still unsafe if copied without the caution comment above it
recommendations.problem: The documented mitigation (child-process retry, BH fallback) is proven to work, but it lives in prose and in examples/, not in the primary code block itself. An agent that copies only `res <- ihw(pvalue ~ mean_expression, data = de_table, alpha = 0.05, nbins = 5)` still has roughly a 50% chance of crashing the analyst's R session on a con table this size, measured directly in this re-audit (6/12).
recommendations.root_cause: The safe pattern is documented as a caution and a pointer to examples/, not embedded as the default code an agent would paste.
recommendations.fix: Make the child-process-wrapped call the primary code block for IHW, with the bare formula call moved into the caution comment as the thing NOT to run directly -- inverting which version an agent is likely to copy first.

recommendations.title: The shipped example's BH step still teaches the wrong lesson
recommendations.problem: examples/multiple_testing_correction.R, run seven times in this re-audit, consistently prints a realized FDR of 0.108 for BH at nominal 0.05 on its fixed seed -- unchanged from the pre-fix audit, and explicitly left unfixed per the fix log's own scope note.
recommendations.root_cause: The fixer correctly deprioritized this as requiring a data-generator change outside the P1 fix pass's scope.
recommendations.fix: Average the method-comparison table over a few replicate seeds, or pick a seed nearer the median of the FDP distribution, so the shipped example does not appear to show its own recommended method failing by 2x.

recommendations.title: Local FDR and IDR remain underspecified relative to what the description promises
recommendations.problem: qobj$lfdr is computed with no threshold-interpretation rule (an arbitrary 0.20 cutoff returned 987 features at realized FDP 0.0375 in this re-audit's Input 1), and IDR is still one taxonomy row with no code, unchanged from the pre-fix audit.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix pass targeted the four flagged P1s; this gap was not one of them and was not touched.
recommendations.fix: Either add a conventional lfdr cutoff convention and a concrete IDR entry point, or trim those promises from the frontmatter description to match the body's actual coverage.
